text: My 17-year-old son, Jackson, weighs 220 pounds and has hypertension, high cholesterol, and sleep apnea. He's been prescribed medications for his conditions, but they're not working as well as expected. His doctor suggested bariatric surgery as an option. What are the potential risks and benefits of bariatric surgery for him?

Hello doctor, I am 45 years old and have been on metformin for polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) for the past five years. Recently, I started experiencing heavy and irregular menstrual bleeding. Could this be related to my PCOS or hormonal imbalance?

My 6-year-old grandson was playing outside last week and scraped his knee on a rusty metal fence. It was a pretty deep cut, so we cleaned it with soap and water. Now, the area is red, swollen, and oozing a yellowish pus. He also has a fever of 101°F. I’m wondering if this is just an infection from the cut, or could it be something more serious like tetanus? He’s never had a tetanus shot since we moved here and aren’t sure about his immunization history.

I’m a 60-year-old retired man with COPD, on home oxygen at 2 L/min, who’s recently developed worsening shortness of breath and confusion. I’ve been taking albuterol and tiotropium inhalers as prescribed, but my symptoms seem different—more persistent even after using my rescue inhaler. My wife says I’ve been acting 'off' the past few days, like I’m not making sense when I talk. I’ve never smoked, but I worked in a factory for 30 years where we used solvents and cleaning chemicals. Could this be from chemical exposure at work years ago finally catching up to me? I’ve also been taking acetaminophen for joint pain since my arthritis flared up last month.

I’m a 72-year-old woman with stage 4 chronic kidney disease, on hemodialysis three times a week. I also have severe osteoporosis and recently fractured my wrist. I’m scheduled for an ORIF (open reduction and internal fixation) next week. My creatinine is 4.8 mg/dL and potassium is 5.2 mEq/L. I take sevelamer, calcitriol, and furosemide. How will my kidney disease affect my anesthesia? Will they have to give me a special kind of anesthesia because my kidneys don’t work well? I’m terrified of waking up with worse kidney function or needing dialysis more often.

I'm a 30-year-old man who has been feeling off for about 2 months. I've had a fever that comes and goes, sometimes up to 101°F, and my joints, especially my knees and ankles, have been really achy. I've lost about 8 pounds without trying, and I have this weird rash on my arms and legs that looks like little red dots—some look like tiny bruises. I don't smoke or drink much, and I'm not sexually active. My only medication is a multivitamin. I saw my doctor last week, and they said it might be a virus, but I'm worried it's something more serious like lupus or another autoimmune disease.

Hello doctor, my 12-year-old son has been experiencing severe toothache in his upper right molar for the past three days. He's also been experiencing fever and swelling of the gum. Can you recommend any treatment options for my child's condition?

I’m a 60-year-old man with type 2 diabetes for 10 years, currently on metformin 1000mg twice daily and linagliptin 5mg daily. Since adding linagliptin three months ago, I’ve developed a persistent dry cough that doesn’t seem related to allergies or a cold. It’s worse at night and interferes with my sleep. My blood sugars are well-controlled. Could this be a side effect of linagliptin, or should I look for another cause?

I’m a 68-year-old retired man with a history of hypertension and heart disease. I’ve been taking 4 extra-strength Tylenol tablets (500mg each) every 4-6 hours for chronic knee pain over the past 2 months. Lately, I’ve felt nauseous, my skin has turned yellowish, and my urine is darker than usual. Am I at risk for liver damage from the acetaminophen? What should I check?

My 5-year-old daughter has been coughing nonstop for two weeks now. It started with a cold, but the cough never went away—it’s worse at night and sometimes ends with her vomiting. She has no fever currently, but she sounds like she’s barking when she coughs. She’s had this before when she was 3, and they said it was croup, but the pediatrician this time prescribed an albuterol inhaler with no improvement. What could this be? I’m really worried it’s something serious.

I'm a 24-year-old college student with a history of seasonal allergies who developed persistent sinus congestion and facial pressure about 6 weeks ago. It started after a cold, and I've tried over-the-counter loratadine, fluticasone nasal spray, and even used a neti pot with no improvement. My primary care doctor prescribed a 2-week course of doxycycline which helped partially but the congestion returned after stopping. I'm concerned this might be a sinus infection that keeps coming back. What are my treatment options for chronic sinusitis, and could this be something more serious like nasal polyps?

Hello doctor, I'm a 28-year-old female who just got my wisdom teeth taken out last week. I'm experiencing some bleeding, and I'm worried that it might be a sign of something serious. I've been following my dentist's instructions and taking the prescribed pain medication. However, I'm also taking a new multivitamin that my mother suggested. Can you please tell me if there's anything I should be concerned about?

I’m a 55-year-old male who had a heart attack 3 weeks ago and required a stent placement, followed by a 5-day ICU stay for cardiogenic shock. I’m now home, but I’m still extremely tired—so much so that I can’t even shower without needing to lie down for an hour afterward. My heart rate jumps to 120 bpm when I stand up, and I feel lightheaded. My doctor says my heart function is improving (ejection fraction is now 45%), but I’m worried this isn’t normal. I’m on metoprolol, lisinopril, and a statin, but I’m not sure if these are helping. What could be causing this persistent fatigue and tachycardia?

I'm a 19-year-old college student who woke up yesterday with a rash on my torso. It started as a few small red spots but has spread to my arms and legs now. The spots are pinkish-red, flat, and slightly itchy. I also have a mild fever, headache, and feel like my lymph nodes are swollen. I haven't been around anyone sick recently, but I did have unprotected oral sex about a week ago. I'm worried this might be related to an STI. What are the chances this is secondary syphilis?

I’m a 24-year-old woman who noticed a lump in my right breast about 2 months ago. It’s painless but feels hard and doesn’t move when I press on it. My periods are regular, and I don’t have a family history of breast cancer. I took a home pregnancy test last week, which was negative. I started a new birth control pill (drospirenone/ethinyl estradiol) about 3 months ago. Could this be cancer? Should I wait to see if it goes away, or should I get it checked now?

Doctor, I'm a 58-year-old woman recently diagnosed with fibromyalgia after years of widespread muscle pain, fatigue, and sleep disturbances. I've tried physical therapy, acupuncture, and gabapentin, but the pain is still interfering with my daily activities. I'm now considering adding a low-dose antidepressant like amitriptyline, but I'm hesitant because I don't feel depressed—will this help my pain, and are there alternative options that might work better for me?

Hello doctor, I'm a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing recurring urinary tract infections (UTIs) over the past year. I've been taking antibiotics as prescribed, but the symptoms persist. I'm also experiencing some discomfort during sex and spotting between periods. I've been taking an oral contraceptive pill for contraception. I want to know what diagnostic procedures might be necessary to determine the cause of my UTIs and other symptoms.

I'm a 45-year-old female who has been dealing with interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome (IC/BPS) for the past 3 years. My symptoms include chronic pelvic pain, urgency, frequency (up to 20 times a day), and occasional nocturia. I've tried dietary modifications (elimination diet, low-acid foods), physical therapy for pelvic floor dysfunction, and oral pentosan polysulfate, but my symptoms remain severe. My pain specialist suggested trying intravesical lidocaine instillations, but I'm skeptical about the procedure. I also take gabapentin for chronic pain and duloxetine for depression, which helps somewhat with the pelvic pain but not the urinary symptoms. What other treatments should I consider, and is there a role for bladder hydrodistension in my case?

I'm a 70-year-old retired nurse who’s been experiencing intermittent but worsening shortness of breath over the past year, especially when climbing stairs. I also have a dry cough that wakes me up at night and unintentional weight loss of about 15 pounds over 6 months. My past medical history includes well-controlled atrial fibrillation on metoprolol, mild COPD, and osteoarthritis. My primary care doctor ordered a CBC that showed a hemoglobin of 9.8 g/dL (normal 12-16) and a mean corpuscular volume (MCV) of 110 fL (high), but the rest of the counts, including white blood cells and platelets, were normal. My iron, B12, and folate levels were normal. What could be causing this anemia, and what tests should come next?

I'm a 72-year-old woman who started taking tolterodine for overactive bladder symptoms about 2 months ago. In the last few weeks, I’ve been feeling very confused at times, especially in the evening, and I’ve had trouble urinating completely. I’m also experiencing more constipation. Could this be from the medication? I’ve never had confusion before.

I’m a 35-year-old man who recently started a new relationship and had unprotected sex about 2 weeks ago. Last week, I noticed a painless sore on my penis that went away after a few days. Now, I have a non-itchy rash on my palms and soles of my feet, along with fatigue and a low-grade fever (99.5°F). I’m terrified I might have syphilis or HIV. I read that the sore could be a chancre, but I’m not sure. I’ve been feeling anxious and haven’t told my partner yet. Should I get tested for syphilis, and could this be HIV seroconversion? What about other sexually transmitted infections (STIs)?

I’m a 55-year-old male with a history of hypertension and kidney disease (Stage 3a, eGFR 55). My blood pressure has been poorly controlled on lisinopril 20mg daily, and my cardiologist recently added amlodipine 5mg. My BMI is 28, and I’ve been told to cut back on salt, but I’m struggling because I love processed foods. My dietary intake includes canned soups, deli meats, and frozen pizzas. Last month, my blood pressure was 155/95, and my potassium was slightly elevated. What are my alternatives besides just reducing salt intake?

I'm a 68-year-old woman who had a hip replacement surgery two weeks ago. Over the past five days, I've developed a low-grade fever (around 100.5°F), some swelling around the incision, and I'm feeling more fatigued than usual. I'm also on blood thinners for a prior pulmonary embolism. Should I be concerned about an infection, or is this just part of the normal recovery process? I'm worried it might be affecting my incision healing, especially since I've been taking my antibiotics as prescribed.

I’m a 45-year-old male with no significant past medical history. For the past year, I’ve noticed a small, painless lump near the base of my penis, just below the head. It’s about the size of a pea and doesn’t change with erections or urination. I’m worried it might be Peyronie’s disease, but I don’t have any curvature. Could this still be related, and what other conditions should I be concerned about? I’m also experiencing some mild discomfort during sex occasionally.
